nations.name: Kaw Nation
nations.lands: Oklahoma, with historical homelands in Kansas and the Great Plains

facts.text: The Nation's history describes forced cession of its Kansas lands and removal to Indian Territory, where the Kanza had to buy their new land.
facts.evidence: forced the tribe to cede all lands in Kansas

facts.text: The Nation's history distinguishes a Tribal Council from a General Council composed of enrolled adult citizens.
facts.evidence: a Tribal Council (executive body) and a General Council

facts.text: The Nation's government history records a vote accepting a new constitution in 2011.

source.title: History Of The Government Of The Kaw Nation

facts.evidence: voted 58 percent to 42 percent to accept

facts.text: The Nation's language page lists online learning and a basic Kanza course. Listed materials remain under the publisher's access and use conditions.
facts.evidence: online courses and downloadable documents regarding Kanza Language education

nations.name: Otoe-Missouria Tribe
nations.lands: Red Rock, Oklahoma; historical homelands include Nebraska and the lower Missouri River valley

facts.text: The Tribe's history dates confinement on a Big Blue River reservation in southeast Nebraska to 1855.
facts.evidence: reservation on the Big Blue River in southeast Nebraska

facts.text: The Tribe's history records removal to Red Rock, Oklahoma, in 1881, followed by boarding-school pressure on children and language.
facts.evidence: In 1881 they were moved to Red Rock, Oklahoma

facts.text: The Tribe's government page describes a seven-member Tribal Council elected by qualified Tribal voters using a secret ballot.
facts.evidence: seven members elected by secret ballot by qualified voters

facts.text: The Tribe's preservation page dates National Park Service recognition of its Tribal Historic Preservation Office to spring 2016.
facts.evidence: formally recognized by the NPS in the Spring of 2016
